reviewed_by: Claude Opus 5 blind reviewer, re-review after the conversion gate and cm ceiling, 2026-08-13

samples_reviewed.question_text: A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?

Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.

How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Seven of the sixteen seeds are not answerable from what the stem says: seeds 44, 45, 50, 501 and 502 read 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' and seeds 68 and 500 read 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.', with no object named and nothing depicted in the sample, so the student has nothing to measure. On the two verbs the sentence names, measure is never really exercised even in the perimeter items, because seeds 42, 43, 46, 603 and 604 hand over every side in the text; identify is reached only implicitly at seed 601, 'How much fencing is needed to go all the way around it?'.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Inside the perimeter items the figure set is reasonable: seed 42 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm.', seed 43 'A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm.', seed 603 'A square has a side of 3 cm.' and the contextual case at seed 601. But only 6 of 16 seeds are perimeter at all, no seed asks the student to obtain the side lengths with a measuring tool before adding them, and no seed works backwards from a given perimeter to a missing side.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Arithmetic stays inside Grade 2 Quarter 4. The largest total is at seed 43, 'A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm.', answered 34 by repeated addition rather than by any formula, and seed 603 totals 12. No multiplication is required, no decimals or fractions appear, and no later-grade vocabulary is used; seed 605 offers the Grade 2 choice 'centimeters or meters?', which is within reach at this quarter.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three formatters appear (mcq, cloze, read_mcq) over several distinct stem families: bare-figure perimeter at seeds 42, 43, 46, 603 and 604; a real-world context at seed 601, 'A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide.'; unit selection at seed 605; and comparison at seed 607, 'Which distance is longer?'. Options are near-miss values around the key rather than repeats, and the key position moves between A, B, C and D across seeds.

competency_alignment.rationale: The sentence is about the perimeter of a plane figure, yet ten of the sixteen seeds address something else entirely: the length of a single unnamed object (seeds 44, 45, 50, 68, 500, 501, 502), unit selection at seed 605, 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the barangay hall and the plaza', magnitude comparison at seed 606, 'Which is longer: 1 cm or 6 cm?', and distance comparison at seed 607. None of those involves a plane figure or the boundary around it, so the majority of the pool sits outside the competency this node maps to.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Magnitudes suit the tool implied. Measured objects run from 5 cm to 82 cm, all under a metre and within reach of a metre stick, while the large distances correctly switch units: seed 601 'A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide.' and seed 605 keying 'm' for a barangay hall to plaza distance. Both triangles can exist under the triangle inequality: seed 42 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm.' has 1 plus 2 greater than 2, and seed 604 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm.' has 2 plus 4 greater than 4.
